name: Randa Duncan Williams
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Randa Duncan Williams chairs Enterprise Products Partners, the pipeline giant her father Dan Duncan (d. 2010) founded in 1968.
Williams is the only one of four siblings involved in running the family business; all four inherited stakes in the company.
Enterprise Products owns over 50,000 miles of energy pipelines, natural gas processing plants and a large oil storage facility on the Gulf Coast.
Williams joined the family business in 1994 and became president and CEO of Enterprise Products in 2001.
She sits on the board of trustees at Rice University, where she got her bachelor's degree in 1985.
forbes_facts: With a law degree from the University of Houston, Williams practiced law for about 6 years beginning in 1988, handling toxic tort cases and property liability cases.
Her father Dan Duncan became the first American billionaire to pass his fortune tax-free to his descendants due to a temporary repeal of the estate tax law in 2010.

name: Bret Taylor
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)
forbes_bio: Bret Taylor is the CEO of Sierra, an AI startup that makes customer service agents.
Taylor is a prominent executive in Silicon Valley, with notable stints at Google, Facebook, Salesforce.
He is the board chairman at OpenAI, in addition to leading Sierra.
In September, Sierra raised $350 million, led by Greenoaks Capital, valuing the startup at $10 billion.

name: Deng Weiming
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)
forbes_bio: Deng Weiming chairs CNGR Advanced Material, which makes components of lithium batteries, some of which are used in cars.
Customers include U.S.-based Tesla, Korea-based LG Chem and China-based CATL.
Deng started his own business in 1995 age 27; he founded CNGR in 2004.
CNGR Advanced Material listed on Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2020 and Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2025.

name: Charles Liang
sec_insider_companies: Super Micro Computer, Inc. (SMCI) - President and CEO
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Charles Liang and his wife Sara Liu founded AI server and storage maker Super Micro Computer Inc. (commonly known as Supermicro) in 1993.
Liang has served as CEO, president and chairman of the board at Supermicro since the company's founding; Liu is senior vice president.
Headquartered in San Jose, California, Supermicro is a major supplier of Nvidia for AI server design outsourcing.
Liang was born in the southern city of Chiayi, Taiwan.
forbes_facts: Liang holds several patents for his server technologies.
Liang is the founder and CEO of the Green Earth Foundation, which aims to combat deforestation.
